description: In the live preview, let me hide or show individual pieces, e.g. hide the top plate or a housing to see how the gears mesh inside, without needing the full exploded view. Use a per-part visibility toggle (eye icon) in a parts list, plus optional 'isolate this part', and keep it working with the open/close animation so I can watch the gears move. Related: voice-a5d65841 (per-part version pickers, same preview UI).

results.identified_issue: Visibility is mesh.visible keyed by model.name in view.hiddenParts (per tile, in memory, not saved like hidden.json). Framing (Box3.setFromObject) still counts hidden meshes on purpose, so the camera doesn't jump. A shared makeMesh() helper now builds meshes for both updateView and requestTune, and it stores userData.name and userData.color. showParts(view) runs after every mesh swap. partsTarget() = the focused view if it has more than 1 part, else the first visible view with more than 1 part (opening it focuses that view, and unfocusing closes the sheet). Tested with Playwright in node 20 against a symlinked copy of ~/HelpingHands-tools/design-gallery. I didn't test on a physical phone. Phone header crowding is a pre-existing issue, made a bit worse by the extra button.
results.summary: Added a Parts panel to the live preview: an eye per part to hide or show it, Only to isolate one, and hidden parts keep moving with Open/Close
results.detailed_description: There's a new Parts button in the preview's header. It opens a side sheet (the bottom half of the screen on a phone) that lists every part of the tile you're looking at, e.g. Left finger, Right finger, Left/Right handle-gear, Pinion, Base, Top plate, Motor for the mix tile. Tap the eye to hide a part. Tap Only to show just that part, tap it again to bring everything back, and Show all clears every hide. Hiding just makes the mesh invisible, so Open/Close and Explode still move the hidden parts and the camera stays where it is. Hide Top plate and Motor, press Close, and you can watch the pinion turn the handle-gears. The phone layout keeps the Open/Close button visible above the sheet for this. Each tile remembers what you hid when you change pickers, when the catalog refreshes, or when Tune re-renders the parts. The hides reset when the page reloads. For links and screenshots, ?hide=top plate,motor presets it (it hides any part whose name contains one of those words). Parts and Tune share the side sheet, so opening one closes the other. I tested it in headless Chromium at desktop and phone sizes with no console errors (screenshot attached: Top plate and Motor hidden, gears showing). It ships once the publisher copies the viewer, within about five minutes. One thing I noticed on a 390 px phone: with '29 hidden' and 'Tune Base 12' also in the header, the project picker shrinks to just its arrow. That was already tight before this change; I can shorten those labels if it bothers you.

summary: The live preview needs a parts list with per-part eye-icon visibility toggles, so users can hide pieces like the top plate or a housing. Hidden parts must stay hidden during the open/close animation, with an optional "isolate this part" action, so the gears can be watched meshing.
